headline: High: Goose’s broad shell/network/write privileges can collide with MinerU’s document ingestion and MCP surfaces, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP, read/write the filesystem, and ingest files; MinerU processes PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server. If MinerU outputs attacker-controlled document text that Goose later treats as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows. The shared filesystem/MCP bridge makes this more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into Goose prompts or MCP messages without sanitization
IF a shared workspace is used to pass extracted document text between the agents
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt for Goose
Strip executable-looking directives from MinerU output before handoff
Use a read-only handoff directory for extracted text
Require human review before Goose acts on MinerU-derived content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, has broad network egress, and handles provider keys; MinerU ingests local documents and exposes API/MCP surfaces. In a shared workspace, sensitive file contents can flow from Goose into MinerU or vice versa, and Goose’s network egress increases the chance of unintended external transmission. The pair therefore has a default-path leakage risk.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or mounted workspace
IF Goose is configured to send context or files to external model providers
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable network egress for Goose when handling sensitive files
Redact secrets before passing documents to MinerU
Use least-privilege API keys for any external provider calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; MinerU is read-only on files but can still operate concurrently through its API/MCP surfaces. The main conflict is not direct overwrite of the same files by MinerU, but Goose can mutate shared inputs or outputs while MinerU is reading them, causing racey or inconsistent results. Uncertainty about orchestration pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Goose and MinerU operate on the same working tree or input directory
IF no external locking or copy-on-write staging is used
mitigations: Stage inputs into per-agent temp directories
Freeze git state before MinerU reads files
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Run Goose and MinerU in separate containers or users

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or operational actions from MinerU’s extracted text, and MinerU’s document parsing output can be treated as authoritative downstream. Because Goose has shell, git, and network authority, a parsing error or hallucinated extraction can cascade into irreversible commits, commands, or external requests. This is a default-path danger unless explicit verification is added.
conditions: IF Goose consumes MinerU extraction results as facts without verification
IF Goose is allowed to act on those facts via shell, git, or network tools
mitigations: Require source-document citations for every extracted claim
Insert a verification step before Goose acts on MinerU output
Limit Goose to draft-only mode for MinerU-derived tasks
Disable automatic commits or outbound requests on first-pass extraction

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU advertises private/offline operation, while Goose explicitly uses configured model providers and handles provider keys. If regulated or residency-bound documents are processed through Goose after MinerU extraction, data can leave the offline boundary and create a policy mismatch. The compliance issue is driven mainly by Goose; MinerU is cited to show the originating document flow.
conditions: IF regulated documents are passed from MinerU into Goose for downstream reasoning
IF Goose is connected to a non-compliant external provider for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated documents inside MinerU-only workflows
Use a residency-approved provider for Goose
Add a data-class gate before any Goose handoff
Log and review every cross-boundary transfer
